# A compile is keyed on the export data of its imports. A function body the
# export data does not carry recompiles only its own package, and the program
# relinks. A change to the export data recompiles the importers.

env GOCACHE=$WORK/gocache

go build -x -o prog$GOEXE .
stderr 'compile( |\.exe).* -p example/dep '
stderr 'compile( |\.exe).* -p example/mid '
stderr 'compile( |\.exe).* -p main '
go run .
stdout '^one$'

cp body/dep.go dep/dep.go
go build -x -o prog$GOEXE .
stderr 'compile( |\.exe).* -p example/dep '
! stderr 'compile( |\.exe).* -p example/mid '
! stderr 'compile( |\.exe).* -p main '
stderr 'link( |\.exe)'
go run .
stdout '^two$'

cp export/dep.go dep/dep.go
go build -x -o prog$GOEXE .
stderr 'compile( |\.exe).* -p example/dep '
stderr 'compile( |\.exe).* -p example/mid '
go run .
stdout '^three$'

-- go.mod --
module example

go 1.27
-- main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example/mid"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(mid.Value())
}
-- mid/mid.go --
package mid

import "example/dep"

func Value() string {
	return dep.Value()
}
-- dep/dep.go --
package dep

func Value() string {
	return value()
}

//go:noinline
func value() string {
	return "one"
}
-- body/dep.go --
package dep

func Value() string {
	return value()
}

//go:noinline
func value() string {
	return "two"
}
-- export/dep.go --
package dep

func Value() string {
	return "three"
}

//go:noinline
func value() string {
	return "two"
}
